items.readable_text:
Content:
Two expressions involving fractions are equivalent if they are the same.

Content:
Even if two expressions initially appear different, they might still be equivalent. For example, the expressions [MATH: \dfrac{1}{2}x] and [MATH: \dfrac{x}{2}] both represent the same thing: "half of [MATH: x.]" Consequently, they are equivalent.

Content:
We can also see that these expressions are equivalent because [MATH: \dfrac{1}{2}x] can be transformed into [MATH: \dfrac{x}{2}.] Writing [MATH: x] as [MATH: \dfrac{x}{1},] we can multiply [MATH: \dfrac 1 2] and [MATH: \dfrac x 1] using fraction multiplication, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: (1)/(2)x|= (1)/(2) ⋅ x; = (1)/(2) ⋅ (x)/(1); = (1 ⋅ x)/(2 ⋅ 1); = (x)/(2)]

sections.normalized_html:
Writing [MATH: a] as [MATH: \dfrac{a}{1},] we have

[MATH: (2)/(3)a|= (2)/(3) ⋅ a; = (2)/(3) ⋅ (a)/(1); = (2 ⋅ a)/(3 ⋅ 1); = (2a)/(3).]

Thus, the expressions [MATH: \dfrac{2}{3}a] and [MATH: \dfrac{2a}{3}] are equivalent.

Example Prompt:
Find an expression that's equivalent to [MATH: \dfrac{2}3 a.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Writing [MATH: a] as [MATH: \dfrac{a}{1},] we have

[MATH: (2)/(3)a|= (2)/(3) ⋅ a; = (2)/(3) ⋅ (a)/(1); = (2 ⋅ a)/(3 ⋅ 1); = (2a)/(3).]

Thus, the expressions [MATH: \dfrac{2}{3}a] and [MATH: \dfrac{2a}{3}] are equivalent.

key_prerequisites.name: Multiplying Positive Numbers With Negative Numbers

sections.normalized_html:
First, remember that the product of two negative numbers is a positive number. Thus,

[MATH: -\dfrac{2}9 (-z) = \dfrac{2}{9} z.]

Now, writing [MATH: z] as [MATH: \dfrac{z}{1},] we have

[MATH: (2)/(9)z|= (2)/(9) ⋅ z; = (2)/(9) ⋅ (z)/(1); = (2 ⋅ z)/(9 ⋅ 1); = (2z)/(9).]

Thus, the expressions [MATH: -\dfrac{2}9 (-z)] and [MATH: \dfrac{2z}{9}] are equivalent.

items.readable_text:
Content:
The usual procedure also works in the reverse direction. For example, to find an equivalent expression for [MATH: \dfrac{2(y+1)}5,] we can separate the variable part from the rest of the fraction, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: (2(y + 1))/(5)|= (2 ⋅ (y + 1))/(5 ⋅ 1); = (2)/(5) ⋅ ((y + 1))/(1); = (2)/(5) ⋅ (y + 1); = (2)/(5)(y + 1)]

Example Prompt:

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Pulling out the variable part, we have

[MATH: (2(3 − x))/(5)|= (2 ⋅ (3 − x))/(5 ⋅ 1); = (2)/(5) ⋅ (3 − x)/(1); = (2)/(5) ⋅ (3 − x); = (2)/(5)(3 − x).]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Two expressions involving fractions are equivalent if they are the same.

Content:
Even if two expressions initially appear different, they might still be equivalent. For example, the expressions [MATH: \dfrac{1}{2}x] and [MATH: \dfrac{x}{2}] both represent the same thing: "half of [MATH: x.]" Consequently, they are equivalent.

Content:
We can also see that these expressions are equivalent because [MATH: \dfrac{1}{2}x] can be transformed into [MATH: \dfrac{x}{2}.] Writing [MATH: x] as [MATH: \dfrac{x}{1},] we can multiply [MATH: \dfrac 1 2] and [MATH: \dfrac x 1] using fraction multiplication, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: (1)/(2)x|= (1)/(2) ⋅ x; = (1)/(2) ⋅ (x)/(1); = (1 ⋅ x)/(2 ⋅ 1); = (x)/(2)]

---

Item 2 — Example: Identifying Equivalent Expressions with Positive Terms

Example Prompt:
Find an expression that's equivalent to [MATH: \dfrac{2}3 a.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Writing [MATH: a] as [MATH: \dfrac{a}{1},] we have

[MATH: (2)/(3)a|= (2)/(3) ⋅ a; = (2)/(3) ⋅ (a)/(1); = (2 ⋅ a)/(3 ⋅ 1); = (2a)/(3).]

Thus, the expressions [MATH: \dfrac{2}{3}a] and [MATH: \dfrac{2a}{3}] are equivalent.

---

[MATH: -\dfrac{2}9 (-z) = \dfrac{2}{9} z.]

Now, writing [MATH: z] as [MATH: \dfrac{z}{1},] we have

[MATH: (2)/(9)z|= (2)/(9) ⋅ z; = (2)/(9) ⋅ (z)/(1); = (2 ⋅ z)/(9 ⋅ 1); = (2z)/(9).]

Thus, the expressions [MATH: -\dfrac{2}9 (-z)] and [MATH: \dfrac{2z}{9}] are equivalent.

Item 11 — Tutorial: Expressing a Fraction as a Product

Content:
The usual procedure also works in the reverse direction. For example, to find an equivalent expression for [MATH: \dfrac{2(y+1)}5,] we can separate the variable part from the rest of the fraction, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: (2(y + 1))/(5)|= (2 ⋅ (y + 1))/(5 ⋅ 1); = (2)/(5) ⋅ ((y + 1))/(1); = (2)/(5) ⋅ (y + 1); = (2)/(5)(y + 1)]

---
